land.text: French Chad, granted independence by France on 11 August 1960; Cliopatria carries this land in its French Fifth Republic row for 1958-1960

predecessors.note: The political predecessor is the French Equatorial Africa federation (the french-africa dossier); Cliopatria's French Africa row ends in 1957 and its French Fifth Republic row holds the land to 1960. The Chad page's infobox gives 28 November 1958 as the date autonomy was granted.

capitals.name: Fort-Lamy
capitals.note: The city was the capital under its colonial name: 'Before its renaming in 1973, the city was known as Fort-Lamy'; the history section dates the renaming by President Tombalbaye to 6 April 1973 (N'Djamena page; the lead says 1975). Same site as N'Djamena. Split by the reviewer of af-08-h.

capitals.name: N'Djamena
capitals.note: The Chad page names N'Djamena 'the capital and largest city'. The Chadian-Libyan conflict page says the capital fell on 16 December 1980 to the attack begun on 6 December 1980 and that Habre's rebel factions had taken it in 1979 (Chad page). Named Fort-Lamy until 6 April 1973 (N'Djamena page).

correction.text: Chad in its independence year: the Cliopatria 1961 shape unchanged, from 11 August 1960

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Chad shape begins in 1961, but 'Chad was granted independence on 11 August 1960'. In 1960 Cliopatria still draws the land inside its French Fifth Republic row (4,598 of the 4,602 cells).

correction.text: the shape as drawn for 1961-1972 and from June 1994; for 1973 to May 1994 the Aouzou Strip ('an area of 114,000 km2' in northern Chad) is Libyan-occupied land, and the BET Prefecture is contested in 1978-1981 and 1983-1987 (ledger events)

keyframe_review.note: 1.273 M km2 against the infobox's 1,280,000 km2 and the body's 1,284,000 km2 (ratio 0.99): the shape contains the Aouzou Strip throughout, so it is right in 1961-1972 and from 1994 and over-draws Chad by about 114,000 km2 (9 percent) in 1973-1994, when Libya 'proceeded to occupy and annex' it. Cliopatria's Libyan shapes (1953-2024) do not reach the strip (0 shared cells), so the occupation is drawn nowhere; the ledger's occupation events supply it. The Chad page gives no boundary changes.
Same outline as 1961 at 1.273 M km2; no boundary change after the 1994 handover of the Aouzou Strip is recorded on the pages opened.

region.text: Chad (the whole of the present country, Aouzou Strip included in Chad's claim)

ledger.note: 1960: Chad becomes independent from France. 'Chad was granted independence on 11 August 1960'; the infobox also gives 28 November 1958 for the grant of autonomy.

region.text: the Aouzou Strip, 'a strip of land in northern Chad that lies along the border with Libya ... an area of 114,000 km2'

ledger.note: 1973: Libya occupies the Aouzou Strip. 'Hence, in 1973, Libya proceeded to occupy and annex the mineral-rich area without any Chadian resistance'; the page ties it to an April 1972 agreement between Gaddafi and President Tombalbaye ('In April 1972, Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi came to an agreement with Chadian president Francois Tombalbaye'). Libya is the occupier; Chad is the owner and records the event with the roles reversed.

region.text: the BET Prefecture (Borkou, Ennedi, Tibesti) of northern Chad

ledger.note: February 1978: Faya-Largeau falls and Libya-backed rebels take the north. 'fell on 18 February 1978 after sharp fighting to a force of 2,500 rebels' of Goukouni Oueddei supported by possibly 4,000 Libyan troops; 'Oueddei and the Libyans assumed control of the BET Prefecture'. The infobox dates the conflict from 29 January 1978.

region.text: the BET Prefecture (Borkou, Ennedi, Tibesti) of northern Chad

ledger.note: November 1981: Libyan forces leave Chad proper. 'by 16 November all Libyan forces had left Chad, redeploying in the Aouzou Strip.' The Libyan intervention of December 1980 had taken N'Djamena on 16 December 1980 (same page) and a joint communique was issued in Tripoli by Gaddafi and Goukouni on 6 January 1981.

region.text: the BET Prefecture (Borkou, Ennedi, Tibesti) of northern Chad

ledger.note: June 1983: Libya returns to the north. Faya-Largeau 'fell on 25 June 1983' to a GUNT force with Libyan support; after Habre retook it on 30 July, France drew a 'Red Line' along the 15th parallel (raised to the 16th in 1984) and Libya held 'all the territory north of the Red Line'. The region is the BET Prefecture, an approximation of the land north of that line.

region.text: the BET Prefecture (Borkou, Ennedi, Tibesti) of northern Chad

ledger.note: 11 September 1987: the OAU ceasefire ends the Toyota War. Habre began his reconquest 'on 2 January 1987' at Fada; 'Aouzou fell in August to the FANT, only to be repelled by an overwhelming Libyan counter-offensive'; 'a ceasefire on 11 September'. Libya kept the Aouzou Strip, so the strip stays in the occupation event until 1994.

region.text: the Aouzou Strip, returned to Chad

ledger.note: May 1994: Libya leaves the Aouzou Strip. 'The Aouzou dispute was concluded for good on 3 February 1994' when the ICJ ruled 16 to 1 for Chad; the Libyan withdrawal 'began on 15 April and was completed by 10 May', with the formal transfer on 30 May 1994. The Aouzou Strip page adds that Security Council resolutions 915 and 926 (May and June 1994) set up and wound up the observer group monitoring the withdrawal.

wars.name: Chadian-Libyan conflict

zones.text: the BET Prefecture (Borkou, Ennedi, Tibesti) of northern Chad
the Aouzou Strip, held by Libya from 1973

wars.outcome: Chadian and French victory (infobox): the Toyota War of 1987 drove Libya from the BET Prefecture and ended in the 11 September 1987 ceasefire; Libya kept the Aouzou Strip until 1994.
wars.note: Infobox: 29 January 1978 - 11 September 1987. The page counts four Libyan interventions, 'in 1978, 1979, 1980-1981 and 1983-1987'. Fronts by year: Faya-Largeau 18 February 1978; N'Djamena 16 December 1980; Libyan withdrawal 16 November 1981; Faya-Largeau 25 June 1983 and Red Line 15th then 16th parallel; Fada 2 January 1987 and Aouzou in August 1987.

wars.name: Aouzou Strip dispute

zones.text: the Aouzou Strip, 'an area of 114,000 km2'

wars.outcome: The ICJ decided in February 1994 (16 to 1) for Chad's sovereignty; the Libyan withdrawal was completed by 10 May 1994 and the formal transfer took place on 30 May 1994 (these two dates from the Chadian-Libyan conflict page).
wars.note: 'In 1990, the territorial dispute was referred for adjudication to the International Court of Justice (ICJ).' The Chadian claim rested on an 1899 Anglo-French agreement and a 1955 France-Libya treaty; Libya's on the unratified 1935 Mussolini-Laval agreement.

wars.name: Chadian Civil War
wars.outcome: 'In 1979 the rebel factions led by Hissene Habre took the capital.' The page gives no territorial division.
wars.note: 'In 1965 Muslims in the north, led by the National Liberation Front of Chad' began the civil war. The rebel-held north is not described on the Chad page; it is drawn through the Libyan contest events from 1978. A gap-filler should open 'Chadian Civil War (1965-1979)'.

wars.name: Chad-Sudan war
wars.outcome: 'An agreement for the restoration of harmony between Chad and Sudan, signed 15 January 2010' ended a five-year war; the border reopened after seven years of closure. No territory changed hands.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered.

certainty.note: The northern frontier with Libya is disputed until the 1994 judgment (Chad's claim rested on 1899 and 1955 instruments, Libya's on the unratified 1935 agreement); desert frontiers elsewhere are colonial lines the pages do not date.

The Libyan frontier is fixed by the ICJ judgment of 3 February 1994 and the withdrawal of May 1994; the Lake Chad shoreline stays soft; the pages opened give no instrument for the other frontiers (a judgment, not a source).

sources.title: Chad
sources.note: Independence 11 August 1960, area 1,280,000 / 1,284,000 km2, N'Djamena, the 1965 civil war, 1979 and 1990, the 2010 Chad-Sudan agreement. Silent on the Aouzou Strip and on boundary changes.

sources.title: Aouzou Strip
sources.note: 1973 Libyan occupation, 114,000 km2, the ICJ judgment of February 1994, UN observer resolutions 915 and 926.

sources.title: N'Djamena
sources.note: Added by the af-08-h reviewer: 'Before its renaming in 1973, the city was known as Fort-Lamy'; renamed by Tombalbaye on 6 April 1973 (history section; the lead says 1975).

notes: Budget: 3 pages (the state page and two on the Libyan dispute); the brief allows 1-2 for a state of 2 shapes, taken from the slack of the simpler states of this batch. Cliopatria draws one Chad shape for 1961-2023 that includes the Aouzou Strip, and its Libyan shapes do not reach the strip, so the 1973-1994 occupation is invisible there; the occupation event (Libya the occupier, Chad the owner) and the Libyan dossiers (libyan-arab-republic 1969-2013, which should carry the matching occupation_start) must agree. The BET contest zones are an approximation of 'the north' (Borkou, Ennedi, Tibesti admin-1 units); the Red Line of 1983-1987 ran at the 15th and then the 16th parallel, across the Borkou and Ennedi units. The N'Djamena episode of December 1980 to November 1981 (the capital fell on 16 December 1980 to Goukouni's Libyan-backed forces) is not drawn as a separate contest because Goukouni then headed the recognised GUNT government. Not settled: the Chadian Civil War (1965-1979) territorial picture (page silent); the renaming of Fort-Lamy to N'Djamena (not on the pages); the dates of Habre's 1982 takeover (the Chad page gives 1979 for the capture of the capital and 1990 for Deby). Gazetteer names needed: 'Aouzou Strip'. Counterparts: libyan-arab-republic (1969-2013) is the counterpart of the occupation and contest events; kingdom-of-libya (1953-1968) shares the frontier before 1969. Cliopatria's 1960 land sits in the French Fifth Republic row.
